verdicts.fix_notes: (1) Not every one of the 21 surviving 'wrong labels' is a Newton failure. In my replication the largest error was a deep-ITM call (T=0.025, lm=-0.298) where brentq hit its own 1e-4 floor because the price is about intrinsic plus quadrature noise, so neither value means anything there. Inverting OTM options only (puts via parity for K<F) fixes both cases. The price-accuracy mask must be applied to the parity-derived put price too: Heston call quadrature error (~1e-3 abs) passes straight into the OTM put. (2) Test (c), '90 nodes', contradicts the proposed price mask: with the 03-24 params only 76 nodes have price > 1e-3. Instead assert that every dropped node is logged with a reason and that no node returns a clip value (1e-4 or 5.0). (3) Manaster-Koehler sigma0 = sqrt(2|ln(F/K)|/T) is 0 at K=F, so floor it (e.g. max(sigma0, 0.1)). Keep a per-element bracket and per-element convergence, not the current batch-wide nanmax(|delta|) test, which never fires while any element bounces. Jaeckel's 'Let's be rational' (py_vollib_vectorized) is the reference implementation if a dependency is acceptable. (4) This also changes the published '8.1x speedup': see the missed item hygiene-nn-speedup-inflated. (5) Regenerating greeks_surface: choose explicitly which calibration it represents (see the missed item about the 03-24 pickle using rho=-0.99), and render the as-of date from the parquet's as_of_date column instead of the hard-coded '2026-03-24' badge. (6) Moving the inverter to a torch-free module also removes the accidental torch import chain behind the published backtest Sharpe (missed item hygiene-backtest-kpi-torch-import-chain). Do that before any requirements split.

missed.title: _prepare_spx_surface can select the same expiry for two bucket targets, duplicating 9 anchors (double weight) and inflating n_spx_options
missed.description: For each target in [14,30,60,91,180,365] days, the code takes the closest available expiry within 50% of the target. Nothing stops two targets from choosing the same expiry. That slice's 9 top-vega rows are then appended twice: it is double-weighted in the SPX loss and counted twice in n_spx_options. This matters now that thin chains are the norm, and it defeats any row-count sufficiency gate such as the 'n_spx_options >= 27' proposed in hygiene-selector-headlines-1-expiry-fit.
missed.evidence: I mocked db.get_options_surface in my copy and called _prepare_spx_surface with S=7000. A single 21-day expiry gives 18 rows, 1 unique expiry and 9 duplicated (strike, right, T) rows. Expiries at 21 and 45 days give 27 rows and 2 unique expiries; the 21d slice is selected by both the 14d and 30d targets, giving value_counts {21d: 18, 45d: 9}.
missed.proposed_fix: Track the expiries already used and skip a target whose best_T is already selected; alternatively, match targets to expiries one-to-one. Persist n_spx_expiries = cal_df['time_to_expiry'].nunique() and gate on it. Test: the 21d-only chain yields 9 rows and 1 expiry; the 21d+45d chain yields 18 rows and 2 expiries.

missed.title: Published Greeks surface is built from the 03-24 pickle (rho=-0.99, outside current bounds; SPX RMSE 3.83 > 3.0 gate) while the same-date baseline JSON used by the NN records rho=-0.95
missed.description: Two artifacts that claim to be the same 2026-03-24 fit, with identical losses (spx 3.8334, vix_fut 1.1502, vix_opt 37.1446), disagree on rho: -0.99 in the pickle and -0.95 in the JSON. The Greeks page (static, never regenerated) is built from the -0.99 pickle. That value lies outside the current HESTON_BOUNDS rho floor of -0.95, and is_acceptable_calibration rejects the fit (RMSE 3.83 > 3.0). Meanwhile the calibration page headlines a different (2026-09-25) fit, and the Greeks badge hard-codes '2026-03-24' with no note that the fit fails the system's own gate.
missed.evidence: Rebuilding the surface with the pickle params (rho=-0.99) reproduces 69 nodes, with a median |IV diff| of 4.45e-5 against the published parquet. With the JSON params (rho=-0.95) I get 68 nodes, which does not match. The selector run in my copy marks 2026-03-24 as False (not acceptable). config.HESTON_BOUNDS['rho'] = (-0.95, 0.0). The parquet's as_of_date column reads 2026-03-25 while the page badge says 2026-03-24.
missed.proposed_fix: Decide on one canonical 03-24 record: either correct the JSON to -0.99 or document the clip. When regenerating the Greeks surface after the IV-inverter fix, build it from latest_good_calibration_path() (the same fit the calibration page shows) inside cloud_refresh, and render its as-of date, calibration date and gate status from the parquet's metadata. Test: the Greeks page as-of date equals the calibration page's as-of date.

missed.title: The published '8.1x NN speedup' is measured against a Heston leg that always runs 50 Newton iterations, because non-converging wing elements block the batch early exit
missed.description: _bs_iv_vectorized breaks out of its loop only when max|delta| over ALL valid elements is below tol. In the benchmark's 500-option set, 194 OTM-call elements bounce between the clip values forever, so every timing of the 'Heston + IV inversion' leg pays for all 50 iterations. About half of the benchmarked Heston time is spent in the broken inverter, so the published speedup ratio depends on the bug and will change once the inverter is fixed.
missed.evidence: Best-of-5 perf_counter on the benchmark inputs (seed 42, T=0.25): heston_call_batch 15.9 ms; _bs_iv_vectorized on all 500 options 17.2 ms; on the 306 convergent options 1.07 ms. The Heston leg is therefore about 33 ms, of which the inverter is about 17 ms. A converging inverter would bring it to about 17-18 ms, roughly halving the speedup (estimate; the NN side cannot be timed here because the .pt weights are gitignored).
missed.proposed_fix: After fixing the inverter, re-run nn_pricer.benchmark and update README/substack from its output. Report the Heston pricing and IV-inversion times separately, and report the MAE on all strikes (including K/F > 1.08), not only where the old inverter converged.
